data.title: Structural basis of calmodulin modulation of the rod cyclic nucleotide-gated channel (XL-MS)
data.projectDescription: We used chemical crosslinking mass spectrometry to study the organization and the interaction of the bovine rod outer segment cyclic nugleotide-gated channel with calmodulin. The aims of the study were to identify the D-helix that could not be resolved with cryo-EM and gain further insights into the protein organization.
data.sampleProcessingProtocol: 20 ug of purified CNG channel were crosslinked with calmodulin (CaM) at a 1:2 molar ratio according to a previously published protocol (Leitner et al., Nat Protoc., 2014). Briefly, CaM was added to the purified channel at a saturating concentration of Ca2+ (9 mM) and incubated at 25°C for 10 min. a 1:1 mixture of d-12 labeled and unlabeled DSS (disuccinimidyl suberate) were added and incubated for 1 hour at 25°C. The reaction was quenched by addition of ammonium bicarbonate. Disulfide bonds were reduced with Tris(2-carboxyethyl)phosphine and free cysteines were alkylated with iodoacetamide. The proteins were digested with Lys-C and trypsin overnight. Peptides were desalted via solid-phase extraction and dried in a vacuum centrifuge. The crosslinked peptides were furhter fractionated with peptide-SEC and four fractions were analyzed with LC-MS/MS. Peptides were separated on an Acclaim PepMap RSLC C18 column (250 x 75 um; Thermo Scientific) with a linear gradient from 11-40% B (A: 2% ACN, 0.15% FA; B: 80% ACN, 0.15% FA) over 60 minutes, at a flow rate of 300 nL/min. The samples were acquired in DDA on an Orbitrap Fusion Lumos mass spectrometer (Thermo Scientific) with a 3 sec cycle time and dynamic exclusion of 30 seconds. MS1 Orbitrap resolution was set to 120,000. Charge states between +3 and +7 were selected and the fragmented mass range was set to 350-1500 m/z. Ions were fragmented with collision-induced dissociation in a linear ion trap at a collision energy of 35%.
data.dataProcessingProtocol: Raw files were searched against the bovine proteome and a contaminant database in Spectromine (v.3; Biognosys) first, to generate a FASTA file for crosslinking. All proteins with at least 5% LFQ intensity of the target proteins were retained in the FASTA file for XL-MS analysis. The FASTA file was reversed and shuffled for the generation of a decoy database. The measurements were further analyzed with xQuest v. 2.1.5 (Leitner et al., Nat. Protoc. 2014). Trypsin was selected as the digesting enzymes, with an accepted maximum of 2 missed cleavages. Carbamidylation of cysteines was included as a fixed modification, methionine oxidation was included as a variable modifcation. Crosslinked residues were lysines and protein N-termini. A peptide length of 4-40 amino acids was selected, MS1 tolerance of +/- 15 ppm and MS2 tolerance of +/- 0.2 Da. The data was further analyzed and inspected with xQuest/xProphet viewer. Peptides were filtered with +/- 5 ppm tolerance and a minimum of 3 matched ions, as well as a delta score <0.9. Crosslink types were inspected manually and hits at <5% FDR were accepted. Spectra were manually checked for TIC >= 0.1, 3 sequential or 4 bond breakages within each peptide. Interprotein crosslink identifications were additionally required to be observed at least 3 times.
